st: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and dry them very well with a towel.
Heat [[6 cups]] oil in a heavy pot to 325°F (160°C). Fry the potatoes in batches for 5 minutes, until soft and pale. Drain on a rack.
Make the gravy by melting [[3 tbsp]] butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in [[3 tbsp]] flour and cook for 2 minutes until light brown.
Slowly whisk in [[2 cups]] beef stock until smooth. Add [[1 tsp]] Worcestershire sauce and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Simmer the gravy for 8 minutes, whisking now and then, until it coats a spoon. Keep it hot.
Raise the oil to 375°F (190°C). Fry the potatoes again in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Put the hot fries in bowls and scatter the cheese curds over the top.
Pour the hot gravy over the curds so they soften, and serve right away.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together. Press into a disc and chill 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough out to 0.125 inch thick and cut 12 circles to fit a muffin pan.
Press a circle into each muffin cup. Divide the raisins among the shells, if using.
Whisk the brown sugar, melted butter, maple syrup, egg, vanilla and vinegar until smooth.
Spoon the filling into the shells until about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18 minutes until the filling bubbles and the pastry is golden.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then loosen and move to a rack. The filling firms as it cools.
Line an 8 inch square pan with parchment. Melt [[0.5 cup]] butter, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and the cocoa in a bowl set over simmering water, stirring.
Whisk in the beaten egg and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture thickens like custard, so the egg cooks through.
Remove from the heat and stir in the graham crumbs, coconut and walnuts.
Press the base firmly and evenly into the pan. Chill 15 minutes.
Beat [[0.5 cup]] softened butter with the custard powder, [[3 tbsp]] milk and [[2 cups]] powdered sugar until fluffy.
Spread the custard layer over the cold base and chill 20 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with [[1 tbsp]] butter in short bursts in the microwave, stirring in between until smooth. Cool slightly.
Pour the chocolate over the custard layer and tilt to coat. Chill for 30 minutes until set.
Cut into squares with a hot, dry knife. Keep refrigerated.
Put the pork, beef, onion, garlic, potato and [[1 cup]] water in a large pot. Break up the meat with a spoon.
Bring to a simmer, then cook gently for 30 minutes, stirring often, until the potato is soft and most of the water is gone.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, savory, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Make sure the meat is cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Mash the potato into the mixture a little to bind it. Cool the filling completely, about 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Fit one crust into a 9 inch pie plate.
Spoon in the cooled filling and smooth the top.
Cover with the second crust, trim, and crimp the edges. Cut a few steam vents and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 minutes until the crust is deep golden.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing. Serve with ketchup or chutney.

ing: peameal back bacon, sliced 0.5 inch thick
st: Slice the peameal bacon into 8 pieces about 0.5 inch thick, if it is not pre-sliced.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the slices in a single layer, working in batches. Cook for 4 minutes until browned on the bottom.
Flip and cook another 3 to 4 minutes until the pork is cooked through to 145°F (63°C) and the cornmeal is crisp.
Toast the split rolls cut-side down in a dry pan or with a little butter for 1 minute.
Spread [[1 tbsp]] mustard on each roll.
Pile 2 slices of bacon onto each roll, sprinkle with pepper, and close the sandwiches.
Serve right away while the bacon is hot.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] honey into [[1.25 cups]] warm water. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Mix in the egg, oil, [[1 tbsp]] honey and salt. Add the flour and mix to a stiff dough.
Knead for 8 minutes on a lightly floured surface until smooth and firm.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour, until puffy.
Divide into 12 pieces. Roll each into a rope 8 inches long and join the ends into a ring, pressing to seal. Rest 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C). Boil [[8 cups]] water with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] honey. Spread the sesame seeds on a plate.
Boil the bagels 3 or 4 at a time for 1 minute per side. Lift out and dip the tops in the sesame seeds.
Place on a lined baking sheet and bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden brown.
Cool on a rack. Best eaten the same day with cream cheese.
Mix the salt, sugar, [[1 tbsp]] pepper, [[1 tbsp]] coriander, garlic and paprika. Rub it all over the brisket.
Put the meat in a large zip bag or covered dish and refrigerate for 3 days, turning daily. This cure is what gives the flavor.
Rinse the brisket, pat dry, and rub with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] pepper and [[1 tbsp]] coriander.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C). Set the brisket fat-side up on a rack in a roasting pan with [[2 cups]] water in the bottom.
Cover tightly with foil and cook for 4 hours until fork-tender, ideally reaching 200°F (93°C) inside.
Rest, still covered, for 30 minutes.
Slice against the grain into thick slices.
Pile the meat onto rye with plenty of mustard, 4 slices of bread per two sandwiches, and serve warm.
Stir the yeast and a pinch of the dough sugar into [[1 cup]] warm milk. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Add the egg, melted butter, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and salt, then mix in [[3.5 cups]] flour to form a soft dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces. Stretch and flatten each into an oval about 8 inches long, like a beaver tail.
Heat [[6 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry each piece for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until puffed and golden brown.
Drain briefly, then dip in the cinnamon sugar while hot. Serve right away.

ing: smoked ham hock or ham bone
st: Rinse the split peas under cold water and pick out any stones.
Put the peas, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaves and [[8 cups]] water in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then skim off any foam from the top.
Reduce the heat, partly cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring now and then, until the peas have broken down.
Lift out the ham hock and let it cool a few minutes. Pull off the meat, chop it, and discard the bone and fat.
Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the savory and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Return the chopped ham to the pot and simmer 10 minutes. Add water if too thick.
Taste, then add salt as needed, about [[1 tsp]]. Serve hot with crusty bread.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] sugar in a large bowl.
Rub in the cold butter with your fingers until the mix looks like crumbs.
Pour in about [[1 cup]] milk and stir until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
Knead gently on a floured surface 5 or 6 times, then pat into a round about 1 inch thick.
Cut the round into 6 wedges or leave it whole.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the bannock for 8 minutes per side, covered, until deep golden and cooked through in the middle.
Cool a few minutes and serve warm with butter or jam.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter an 8 inch square baking dish.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat [[0.25 cup]] butter with [[0.5 cup]] sugar until creamy. Beat in [[0.75 cup]] milk and the vanilla.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet until just smooth. Spread the batter in the dish.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] maple syrup, [[1 cup]] water and [[2 tbsp]] butter in a saucepan until boiling, then simmer 2 minutes.
Carefully pour the hot sauce slowly over the batter. Do not stir; the batter will rise up through it.
Bake for 35 minutes until the cake is golden and the sauce bubbles around the edges.
Cool for 10 minutes. Serve warm in bowls with the sauce spooned over.

ing: optional; leave out for a virgin Caesar
one wedge plus a wedge for the rim
st: Rub a lime wedge around the rim of a tall glass.
Pour [[1 tsp]] celery salt on a small plate and dip the wet rim into it.
Fill the glass with [[1 cup]] ice.
Add the vodka (leave it out for a virgin version) and the Worcestershire sauce and hot sauce.
Pour in [[4 fl oz]] Clamato juice and add a pinch of pepper.
Stir gently with the celery stalk to mix.
Squeeze in a fresh lime wedge and serve right away.
